gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AT-LP70XBT's and Sony PS-LX3BT's wow-and-flutter and signal-to-noise figures were measured differently (Audio-Technica's weighted, Sony's WRMS), so the same '<0.25%' and the 55-vs-50 dB gap cannot be compared like for like. This could not be confirmed on a maker page.
standout_why: Compared against Turntableverse (rank 1/2, read 2026-11-10). It lists the AT-LP70XBT at '<0.25%' wow and flutter and '>55 dB' S/N, gives no wow-and-flutter or S/N for either Sony, and names no measurement method for any figure. ChatGPT cited What Hi-Fi? best-Bluetooth and Louder best-record-players, but the fetch returned only their titles, so I can't say what they contain. The finding that the two makers use different measurement methods appears new. It scores 1 rather than 2 because it rests on a retailer and a spec aggregator: every maker page (Audio-Technica US/UK, Sony CA/Asia, JBL global/support) returned 403. Turntableverse also already lists aptX Adaptive for the PS-LX3BT, so the codec parity point isn't new.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. By their own spec sheets the AT-LP70XBT and Sony PS-LX3BT are a tie on the numbers ChatGPT used. Both state a <0.25% wow-and-flutter ceiling under different methods, and the 5 dB S/N gap has no stated weighting on either side. Both also list aptX Adaptive, although ChatGPT's cards credit it only to the AT. So the AT-LP70XBT ($299 vs $349.99 on ChatGPT's cards) wins on price and its replaceable VM95-series stylus, not on any measured spec. The page should say this rather than rank on the spec numbers.
